[[Category:Critical thinking]]
[[File:Think about it.png|thumbnail|Don't assume!]]
'''Media literacy''' refers to the capacity to apply [[critical thinking]] to

* access
* understand
* analyse
* evaluate
* create

[[media content]] to

* obtain relevant, accurate and up-to-date factual information,
* form informed opinions,
* share factual information and opinions with different [[audience]]s, minimising bias and maximising ease of comprehension.

<ref>{{#cite:Q2947}}</ref>

== Techniques ==

=== SIFT ===

See [[SIFT method]].

=== Red flag green flag<ref>{{#cite:Q2947}}</ref> ===

[[File:Red flag.png|100px|center]]
==== Red flags: questionnable content ====
* Unclear authorship
* No dating
* Sensational language
** e.g., "EXPOSED", "BETRAYAL"
* No sources
* One-sided/highly unbalanced presentation
* Poor grammar/spelling/formatting: Signs of
** Low effort content-generation: quantity over quality
** Rushed production
** Lack of editorial standard/proof-reading

[[File:False green flags.png|100px|center]]
==== False green flags: assuring but nothing ====

* Confident tone
* Large amount of technical jargon/complex visuals
* Rhetorical shields
** e.g., "A balanced opinion on the issue would be", "Based on my independent analysis"
* Documentary/news style writing
** Propaganda/advertising experts mimic documentary content/news to create [[soft propaganda]] and [[soft advertisement]]s.
* Popularity
** Contents go viral when they are
*** surprising
*** relatable
*** emotional
*** '''not''' necessarily because they are reliable
